policy_title: Support for Veterans and the Armed Forces
stated: Labour will strengthen support for Armed Forces communities by fully enshrining the Armed Forces Covenant into law and establishing an independent Armed Forces Commissioner to improve service life. Veterans will be ensured access to mental health, employment, and housing support. Visa fees will be scrapped for non-UK veterans who have served for four or more years, and their dependents.

source.quote: We will strengthen support for our Armed Forces communities by putting the Armed Forces Covenant fully into law and establishing an independent Armed Forces Commissioner to improve service life. Labour will ensure veterans have access to the mental health, employment, and housing support and in other areas they need. We will also scrap visa fees for non-UK veterans who have served for four or more years, and their dependents.

bearing_set.reason: Explicit commitment to mental health access for veterans addresses a well-documented gap in NHS/specialist provision for this group, earning a direct healthcare verdict.
Explicit employment support for veterans on transition from service bears directly on whether they can secure decent, secure work.
Explicit housing support for veterans — including potential priority access to social/affordable tenure — bears on housing access for this group.

Fully enshrining the Armed Forces Covenant in law creates legally enforceable rights and equal-treatment protections for service personnel and their families, squarely within O9's legal-rights framework.

Policy directly concerns the armed forces: enshrining the Covenant in law, creating a Commissioner, and improving service life conditions affects retention, morale, and military readiness, bearing on the national security & defence posture indicator within O5's explicit scope.

membership_note: This multi-component policy bears on four fundamentals: housing, healthcare, employment, and equal treatment. Fiscal cost (Commissioner, expanded services, visa fee revenue loss) is probably too small in scale to materially move O12. The Commissioner improving service life could theoretically affect military retention and O5 defence posture, but the inferential chain is too long without a stated mechanism linking it to security capability. O2 and O11 are not in scope: the visa fee removal is an equal-treatment measure (O9) rather than a running cost-of-living or tax burden change.
